newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-CHILAVERT SAYS HE'S FIT FOR SUNDAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHILAVERT SAYS HE'S FIT FOR SUNDAY.

text.p: Paraguay's fiery, goalscoring goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert arrived in the Bolivian capital in a chartered private plane on Wednesday and declared himself fit to play in Sunday's World Cup qualifying match.

Chilavet had ruled himself out of the game away to Bolivia immediately after playing for his Argentine club Velez Sarsfield in the South American Supercup final last week, in which he missed a penalty.
"I feel fine and I hope to be part of the team," he said after stepping off the plane chartered by the Paraguayan Football Federation (LPF).

Chilavert, whose very presence on the pitch appears to fire up his own team and intimidate opponents, has been the key figure as Paraguay have moved into second place in the nine-team South American group.
He scored from a free kick as his team drew 1-1 to gain an unlikely away point against Argentina, whose goalkeeper German Burgos he described as "mediocre."

Bolivia, despite the huge advantage of playing their home games at 3,600 metres altitude, have dropped four points in their three games in La Paz so far and have seen their chances of a second consecutive World Cup appearance fade.
